title: Ordinary inverse-image compositor coherence around a commutative cube
statement: For arbitrary strict semilinear coefficient systems and any commutative cube of schemes, the two composites from k1-star p1-star h-star to r1-star c-star i-star built from the specified moduleSquareG comparisons agree. This requires only the six face commutativity equalities, with no properness, openness or pullback assumption; the operations are those of [def-sp-varying-ring-operations] and [def-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-arrows].

source.place: Tags 03D8 and 07A7, normalized inverse-image composition; compositor calculation used in more-etale.tex Tag 0F7F, extended to strict semilinear systems

proof.text: Prove section-normalized direct-image associativity by the coefficientwise formula of modulePComp_existsUnique: the two composites restrict along the same map of iterated fibre products. Use the already proved site_pasting and restriction_pasting helpers from StrictTowerDirectImageCoherence to identify these maps. Apply Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso_assoc and mate_transport to obtain ordinary associativity for exactly moduleGComp. This reproduces the proved ordinary_coherence calculation of SemilinearCompositorCoherence locally, avoiding that module's unrelated proof imports. Invert its natural-isomorphism equation and transport along supplied equalities to obtain cubeComposition_assoc for independently named composites.

Expand a forward square into the forward comparison to its named composite followed by the inverse comparison for the other path. Choose the common total j followed by iU followed by f. Apply the three-arrow associativity equation to the six paths j,iU,f; j,f0,iV; f0prime,g0,iV; iUprime,gprime,f; iUprime,fprime,g; and f0prime,iVprime,g. Postcompose with the invertible comparison from iUprime,gprime,f to the common total; successive inverse-hom cancellations identify the two three-face cube paths. The six face equalities supply all needed transports, whose proofs agree by proof irrelevance.

Identify each forward square with moduleSquareG.inv, and each reversed square with moduleSquareG.hom, using moduleSquareG_eq. Apply the preceding three-face cube equation with f=i, fprime=i1, g=h, gprime=c, iU=r, iUprime=r1, iV=p, iVprime=p1, f0=k, f0prime=k1, g0=a and j=d. Cancel the inverse of the whiskered a,p1,p,h face comparison on the left. This gives exactly the displayed two-face versus four-face equality.

lean.statement:
theorem moduleSquareG_cube
    {U V W Z U₁ V₁ W₁ Z₁ : Scheme.{u}}
    (k : U ⟶ V) (i : W ⟶ Z) (r : U ⟶ W) (p : V ⟶ Z)
    (k₁ : U₁ ⟶ V₁) (i₁ : W₁ ⟶ Z₁) (r₁ : U₁ ⟶ W₁) (p₁ : V₁ ⟶ Z₁)
    (a : V₁ ⟶ V) (h : Z₁ ⟶ Z) (c : W₁ ⟶ W) (d : U₁ ⟶ U)
    (w : k ≫ p = r ≫ i) (w₁ : k₁ ≫ p₁ = r₁ ≫ i₁)
    (wk : d ≫ k = k₁ ≫ a) (wi : c ≫ i = i₁ ≫ h)
    (wp : a ≫ p = p₁ ≫ h) (wr : d ≫ r = r₁ ≫ c) (M : Modules R φ Z) :
    (moduleSquareG R φ k₁ r₁ p₁ i₁ w₁).inv.app ((pull R φ h).obj M) ≫
        (pull R φ r₁).map ((moduleSquareG R φ c i₁ i h wi).hom.app M) =
      (pull R φ k₁).map ((moduleSquareG R φ a p₁ p h wp).hom.app M) ≫
        (moduleSquareG R φ d k₁ k a wk).hom.app ((pull R φ p).obj M) ≫
        (pull R φ d).map ((moduleSquareG R φ k r p i w).inv.app M) ≫
        (moduleSquareG R φ d r₁ r c wr).inv.app ((pull R φ i).obj M)
